questiontext.text: Chemicals which are released at the synaptic junction are called

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Transmission of nerve impulses between adjacent excitable cells at a chemical synapse is mediated by specialized signaling molecules.

Step 2: Synaptic Mechanism and Comparison
When an action potential arrives at the pre-synaptic axon terminal, it causes voltage-gated calcium channels to open. The influx of calcium ions stimulates the synaptic vesicles to fuse with the pre-synaptic plasma membrane and release their stored chemical messengers across the synaptic cleft. These chemical substances are defined as neurotransmitters (such as acetylcholine). In contrast, hormones are chemical messengers secreted directly into the bloodstream by endocrine glands to act on distant target organs. Cerebrospinal fluid is a protective fluid circulating through the brain ventricles and central canal of the spinal cord, and lymph is a component of the lymphatic circulatory system.

Step 3: Conclusion
Therefore, the chemical substances released into the synaptic cleft at the synaptic junction are neurotransmitters.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_NEURAL_CONTROL_AND_COORDINATION_MCQ_Q02 - Potential difference across resting neural membrane

questiontext.text: Potential difference across resting membrane is negative. This is due to differential distribution of the following ions

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Excitable cells such as neurons maintain an electrical resting membrane potential across their plasma membrane, with the inner surface being electrically negative relative to the outer interstitial fluid.

Step 2: Ionic Distribution and Permeability
The generation and maintenance of this electrical resting potential depend predominantly on the differential concentration gradients and selective membrane permeability of sodium ions (\( \mathrm{Na}^{+} \)) and potassium ions (\( \mathrm{K}^{+} \)). In the resting state, the axonal membrane is significantly more permeable to \( \mathrm{K}^{+} \) than to \( \mathrm{Na}^{+} \). Additionally, active sodium-potassium ATPase pumps transport three \( \mathrm{Na}^{+} \) ions outward for every two \( \mathrm{K}^{+} \) ions brought inward. This electrogenic unequal exchange, coupled with the outward diffusion of \( \mathrm{K}^{+} \) through passive leak channels, creates a deficit of positive charge inside the membrane.

Step 3: Evaluation of Other Ions
Ions such as carbonate, calcium, and magnesium do not establish the primary resting electrochemical gradient of the axonal neurolemma.

Step 4: Conclusion
Consequently, the negative potential difference across the resting neural membrane is due to the differential distribution of \( \mathrm{Na}^{+} \) and \( \mathrm{K}^{+} \) ions.

Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Passive ionic leak across the neuronal membrane would naturally dissipate concentration gradients over time unless actively counteracted.

Step 2: Mechanism of Maintenance
The baseline electrochemical concentration gradients are continuously restored and maintained by an active transport mechanism termed the sodium-potassium pump (\( \mathrm{Na}^{+}/\mathrm{K}^{+} \) ATPase), which is an active ion pump. Utilizing metabolic energy from ATP hydrolysis, this pump transports three sodium ions out of the axoplasm and two potassium ions into the axoplasm against their respective concentration gradients.

Step 3: Evaluation of Other Choices
Hormones act as systemic chemical messengers and neurotransmitters mediate synaptic impulse transmission; neither operates directly as the transmembrane molecular machinery maintaining the resting ionic gradient.

Step 4: Conclusion
Hence, the resting membrane potential is maintained by the ion pump.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_NEURAL_CONTROL_AND_COORDINATION_MCQ_Q04 - Regulation of human visceral organ function

questiontext.text: The function of our visceral organs is controlled by

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Internal visceral organs (such as the digestive tract, heart, lungs, and urinary bladder) operate involuntarily and are regulated by the autonomic neural system.

Step 2: Subdivisions of the Autonomic Neural System
The autonomic neural system consists of two major functional divisions that act antagonistically to maintain visceral homeostasis: the sympathetic neural system (which prepares organs for stress and emergency responses) and the parasympathetic neural system (which promotes energy conservation and restorative functions during rest).

Step 3: Role of Somatic Neural System
The somatic neural system transmits impulses from the central nervous system strictly to skeletal voluntary muscles and is not responsible for the involuntary control of visceral organs.

Step 4: Conclusion
Thus, the function of our visceral organs is controlled by the sympathetic and parasympathetic neural system.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_NEURAL_CONTROL_AND_COORDINATION_MCQ_Q05 - Structures involved in knee jerk reflex

questiontext.text: Which of the following is not involved in Knee-jerk reflex?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The knee-jerk reflex (patellar reflex) is an involuntary, rapid monosynaptic stretch reflex mediated at the level of the spinal cord.

Step 2: Analysis of Reflex Arc Components
Tapping the patellar tendon stretches the extensor muscle, activating muscle spindles (proprioceptive stretch receptors). The afferent sensory neuron conducts action potentials directly to the spinal cord via the dorsal root. Within the spinal cord grey matter, the sensory neuron synapses directly onto an alpha motor neuron, which exits via the ventral root to stimulate the extensor muscle to contract. Interneurons are also present in the spinal cord to mediate reciprocal inhibition of the opposing flexor muscle.

Step 3: Evaluation of Higher Centers
Because the complete reflex loop is integrated entirely within the lumbar segment of the spinal cord, conscious processing or control by the brain is not a component of the reflex arc.

Step 4: Conclusion
Therefore, the brain is not involved in the execution of the knee-jerk reflex.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_NEURAL_CONTROL_AND_COORDINATION_MCQ_Q06 - Brain area associated with strong emotions

questiontext.text: An area in the brain which is associated with strong emotions is

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The emotional core of the human brain comprises interconnected subcortical and cortical forebrain nuclei.

Step 2: Limbic System Anatomy and Function
The inner parts of the cerebral hemispheres along with interconnected deep structures—including the amygdala, hippocampus, and associated hypothalamus—constitute the limbic system (or limbic lobe). Together with the hypothalamus, the limbic system is primarily involved in the regulation of sexual behavior, expression of emotional reactions such as excitement, pleasure, rage, and fear, as well as motivation.

Step 3: Functions of Other Brain Regions
The cerebral cortex primarily processes higher sensory, motor, and associational cognitive tasks. The cerebellum integrates motor commands to maintain balance and coordinate posture. The medulla oblongata contains autonomic centers controlling respiration, cardiovascular reflexes, and gastric secretions.

Step 4: Conclusion
Thus, the area in the brain associated with strong emotions is the limbic system.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_NEURAL_CONTROL_AND_COORDINATION_MCQ_Q07 - Vitamin present in visual pigment rhodopsin

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Rhodopsin (visual purple) is the purplish-red photopigment found in the membrane disks of rod photoreceptor cells in the retina, responsible for twilight and scotopic vision.

Step 2: Biochemical Structure
Rhodopsin is a conjugated protein composed of the apoprotein opsin bound to the chromophore retinal. Retinal is the aldehyde derivative of Vitamin A (retinol). Therefore, Vitamin A is the essential chemical constituent necessary for synthesizing retinal in rhodopsin.

Step 3: Conclusion
Consequently, the vitamin present in rhodopsin is Vitamin A (Vit A).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_NEURAL_CONTROL_AND_COORDINATION_MCQ_Q08 - Structures enclosed by human eyeball layers

questiontext.text: Human eyeball consists of three layers and it encloses

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The wall of the human eyeball is composed of three concentric coats: an external fibrous tunic (sclera and cornea), a middle vascular tunic (choroid, ciliary body, and iris), and an internal nervous tunic (retina).

Step 2: Internal Structures and Cavities
These three boundary layers enclose the transparent crystalline lens and two fluid compartments: the aqueous chamber containing aqueous humor (located between the cornea and lens) and the vitreous chamber containing vitreous humor (located between the lens and retina).

Step 3: Evaluation of Other Listed Structures
The cornea and iris are structural parts of the wall layers themselves rather than contents enclosed within the cavities, and the optic nerve is a cranial nerve that exits the posterior aspect of the globe.

Step 4: Conclusion
Hence, the three layers of the eyeball enclose the lens, aqueous humor, and vitreous humor.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_NEURAL_CONTROL_AND_COORDINATION_MCQ_Q09 - Wax secreting gland in ear canal

questiontext.text: Wax secreting gland present in the ear canal is called

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The external auditory canal (meatus) is lined by skin containing fine hairs and specialized secretory cutaneous glands.

Step 2: Gland Structure and Function
These modified apocrine sweat glands are known as ceruminous glands. Along with sebaceous glands, they secrete cerumen (earwax), a waxy substance that lubricates the canal and prevents dust and foreign particles from contacting the tympanic membrane.

Step 3: Evaluation of Other Glands
Standard sweat glands produce a watery secretion for thermoregulation. The prostate gland and Cowper's (bulbourethral) glands are male accessory reproductive glands that contribute to the seminal fluid.

Step 4: Conclusion
Therefore, the wax-secreting gland present in the ear canal is the ceruminous gland.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_NEURAL_CONTROL_AND_COORDINATION_MCQ_Q10 - Internal ear structure responsible for hearing

questiontext.text: The part of internal ear responsible for hearing is

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The internal ear (labyrinth) is organized into two functionally distinct components: an auditory apparatus dedicated to the perception of sound, and a vestibular apparatus dedicated to maintaining bodily equilibrium.

Step 2: Anatomical Specialization
The coiled, snail-shell-like portion of the labyrinth is the cochlea. It contains the organ of Corti located on the basilar membrane, which possesses mechanosensory hair cells that transduce sound-induced mechanical vibrations of the endolymph into auditory nerve impulses.

Step 3: Functions of Other Inner Ear Structures
The semicircular canals, utriculus, and sacculus make up the vestibular apparatus, which is responsible for detecting angular and linear acceleration to maintain balance and posture.

Step 4: Conclusion
Thus, the part of the internal ear responsible for hearing is the cochlea.

questiontext.text: The organ of corti is a structure present in

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The sensory organ responsible for hearing in mammals is the organ of Corti.

Step 2: Anatomical Localization
The organ of Corti is located inside the cochlea of the inner ear. Specifically, it rests on the basilar membrane within the cochlear duct (scala media). It contains auditory receptor hair cells whose stereocilia interact with the overlying tectorial membrane to convert fluid vibrations into nerve impulses transmitted by the cochlear nerve.

Step 3: Comparison with Other Regions
The external ear consists of the pinna and external auditory meatus; the middle ear contains the tympanic membrane and auditory ossicles; and the semicircular canals house cristae ampullares for dynamic equilibrium.

Step 4: Conclusion
Therefore, the organ of Corti is a structure present in the cochlea.
